output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mostly self-inflicted, not Haverlow's fault. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four in week 31, chilled pallets wait about 3 hours 52 minutes (up from 44 minutes) on an unrefrigerated dock averaging 15–17°C. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier; day shifts stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer telematics, which can't be edited, show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open. The "warm" receiving probe readings were keyed hours after unloading, so they measure dock warming. The chambers held temperature. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Do not raise the chargeback or shift volume: it would penalise the wrong party and leave the cause in place. Do not drop night probing. Restore night staffing, or otherwise cap dock-to-chamber time, and monitor it weekly from scan data. Separately, reconcile a sample of Corriebank claims, since their self-certified credits rose from 3 August. Whether over-claiming is happening is still unknown, so don't ask for photo evidence yet. Fix the receiving process first.
